apps.title: Vet Study 2.0
apps.description: A veterinary e-learning companion for keeping revision material close when you are away from your desk.
apps.workflow: Pick one syllabus topic before opening the app. After reading, close it and explain the key points aloud; check gaps against your course outline.
apps.access: Free to install · contains ads. Content availability may change.

apps.title: VetConnect
apps.description: A veterinary drug index for looking up drug and brand information in an Indian practice context.
apps.workflow: Use it to connect a generic drug to its class and indications. Cross-check species, formulation and current product information with your clinical supervisor.
apps.access: Free to install · contains ads. The listing describes offline and online use.

apps.title: MSD Vet Manual
apps.description: A broad veterinary reference for reviewing diseases, diagnostic approaches and clinical background across species.
apps.workflow: Start with a condition from rounds. Read its overview and diagnostic approach, then write a short problem list before discussing the case.
apps.access: Free reference. Download the core content first; some media and features need an internet connection.

apps.title: IVRI Veterinary Clinical Care
apps.description: An Indian field-practice learning aid covering common medicine, gynaecology and surgery presentations.
apps.workflow: Before a supervised field visit, review one common presentation such as bloat or dystocia. Compare the history, examination and differential diagnoses with what you observe.
apps.access: Free to install. Developed by ICAR-IVRI and IASRI; includes clinical explanations and educational procedure videos.

apps.title: 3D Dog Anatomy
apps.description: Explore canine skeletal, muscular and internal anatomy from multiple angles.
apps.workflow: Hide one system, name the exposed structures, then reveal it to check yourself. Pair the model with your dissection or osteology notes.
apps.access: Paid publisher app · Telegram collection link pending.

resources.title: VetBVSc — year-wise notes
resources.description: BVSc subject and year collections, including links to TANUVAS material.
resources.use: Finding a second explanation or a subject collection. Check older course codes against your own outline.
resources.access: Public pages; linked files have their own access settings.

resources.title: Vetscraft — subject explanations
resources.description: Readable veterinary topic explanations across basic, production and clinical subjects.
resources.use: Understanding a difficult concept before returning to your textbook.
resources.access: Public articles; individual courses may have different access terms.

resources.title: Vets Duo — subject lecture notes
resources.description: Subject-based BVSc collections covering basic sciences, animal production and clinical study.
resources.use: Comparing lecture notes and locating TANUVAS-labelled collections.
resources.access: Public directory; availability depends on each linked collection.

resources.title: DrVet — veterinary study archive
resources.description: An archive of subject notes, exam material and veterinary study posts.
resources.use: Looking for older revision posts or question-paper references. Verify the year and original source.
resources.access: Public posts; external files may require separate access.

resources.title: GreatVets — BVSc revision
resources.description: Veterinary notes organised for BVSc study and revision.
resources.use: Getting a concise topic overview. Check any generated explanation against a textbook.
resources.access: Public notes; other features may require an account.

resources.title: MSD Veterinary Manual
resources.description: Veterinary disease overviews, diagnostic background, tables and clinical learning material.
resources.use: Reading around a case after rounds; start with the species and clinical problem.
resources.access: Free web reference. Educational use does not replace clinical supervision.

resources.title: eClinPath — Cornell clinical pathology
resources.description: An online clinical pathology textbook covering interpretation of haematology, chemistry and other laboratory findings.
resources.use: Understanding why a result changes, rather than memorising a reference interval alone.
resources.access: Free educational text; interpret results with the reporting laboratory’s intervals.

resources.title: IVIS — veterinary reading & continuing education
resources.description: Veterinary proceedings, publications and learning resources from an international education network.
resources.use: Reading more deeply about a clinical question or preparing a seminar.
resources.access: Free registration may be required; access varies by item.

resources.title: PubMed — find the original paper
resources.description: A biomedical literature search service that includes veterinary and comparative research.
resources.use: Finding a primary study. Add species and study design to your search; read methods before trusting a conclusion.
resources.access: Free search and abstracts; full-text availability depends on the publisher.

resources.title: WOAH — animal health codes & manuals
resources.description: International standards and manuals for animal health, diagnostic testing, welfare and veterinary public health.
resources.use: Looking up the official context for disease control, surveillance or diagnostic standards.
resources.access: Public standards; use the current edition and relevant chapter.

resources.title: VCI — veterinary education & registration rules
resources.description: The official collection of veterinary legislation, registration regulations and education standards.
resources.use: Checking the source behind a curriculum or registration claim.
resources.access: Public regulations; use your university’s current implementation as well.

resources.title: IVRI — postgraduate study information
resources.description: Official information about master’s study and veterinary disciplines at IVRI.
resources.use: Shortlisting postgraduate subjects and checking the institution’s current admission route.
resources.access: Public information; the current admission notice determines eligibility and dates.

careers.title: Companion-animal practice
careers.summary: Consults, prevention, diagnostics and follow-up for pets.
careers.work: General practice combines examination, owner communication, treatment planning and records. Emergency or specialist work adds further training and different working hours.
careers.entry: Complete BVSc & AH, the required internship and applicable registration before practising. An MVSc can deepen a field; it is not a universal condition for every general-practice job.
careers.fit: You like case continuity, hands-on work and explaining decisions to worried people.
careers.first: Observe a full clinic shift with permission. Ask who supervises new graduates and how difficult cases are escalated.
careers.watch: A busy caseload is not the same as good mentorship. Ask about night duty, equipment access and protected learning time.

careers.title: Livestock & dairy herd health
careers.summary: Work with individual animals and the performance of a whole herd.
careers.work: Field visits may involve reproduction, mastitis prevention, nutrition, disease surveillance and farmer education. The work connects health decisions to farm management.
careers.entry: BVSc & AH and applicable registration are central to clinical work. Employers may value field experience or postgraduate training in the relevant discipline.
careers.fit: You enjoy farms, travel, practical problem solving and working with livestock owners.
careers.first: Join supervised farm rounds. Practise taking a structured herd history and interpreting production records.
careers.watch: Plan for travel, biosecurity and emergency work. Learn to communicate a workable prevention plan, not just a diagnosis.

careers.title: Poultry, feed & production systems
careers.summary: Prevent disease and improve health at flock or enterprise scale.
careers.work: Roles can include farm health, biosecurity, hatchery support, nutrition, feed technical services and production data review. Some are clinical, others focus on operations or technical support.
careers.entry: Requirements differ by employer. BVSc skills are relevant; targeted MVSc study or practical production exposure can strengthen a specialist application.
careers.fit: You like prevention, systems, numbers and decisions affecting many animals.
careers.first: Visit a production unit through your college. Learn its biosecurity flow and choose one performance indicator to understand.
careers.watch: Check whether a role involves clinical decisions, sales targets, frequent travel or farm residency before accepting.

careers.title: Government veterinary services
careers.summary: Animal health programmes, field services and regulatory responsibilities.
careers.work: Depending on the post, work may involve dispensaries, vaccination programmes, surveillance, extension or administration. State and central posts have different recruitment rules.
careers.entry: Read the exact state PSC, department or UPSC advertisement. Recognised qualifications, registration, age, language and experience requirements vary; some central vacancies are deputation posts.
careers.fit: You value public service, livestock outreach and working within an administrative system.
careers.first: Read one current advertisement end to end. Make a checklist of eligibility, syllabus, documents and the official application portal.
careers.watch: There is no single nationwide “veterinary officer exam” covering every post. Use official notices for deadlines and selection stages.

careers.title: Public health, food safety & One Health
careers.summary: Protect animal and human health through prevention and surveillance.
careers.work: Work may involve zoonoses, food hygiene, outbreak investigations, epidemiology or public health projects. Food safety roles and clinical veterinary posts do not share one eligibility rule.
careers.entry: A relevant MVSc, MPH or epidemiology training may help for particular roles. Verify whether the actual vacancy accepts your degree and requires additional experience or registration.
careers.fit: You enjoy population-level questions, field investigation, data and teamwork across disciplines.
careers.first: Turn a public health topic into a short evidence brief: define the population, risk, data source and practical prevention measure.
careers.watch: An additional degree is useful only when it fits the role. Check recognised entry requirements before paying for a programme.

careers.title: Diagnostics & laboratory medicine
careers.summary: Make laboratory findings useful to the clinician or herd team.
careers.work: Diagnostic work spans pathology, microbiology, parasitology, sample handling, quality control and interpretation. Research laboratories and clinical diagnostic services have different responsibilities.
careers.entry: Supervised laboratory experience is a useful start. Specialist interpretation, research and leadership posts often ask for relevant postgraduate training or experience.
careers.fit: You enjoy detail, methodical work and explaining the limits of a test.
careers.first: Spend time in your teaching laboratory. Follow one sample from collection and transport through reporting and interpretation.
careers.watch: Strong sample quality and quality assurance matter as much as identifying a slide. Avoid treating a test result as a diagnosis on its own.

careers.title: Teaching & research
careers.summary: Ask a better question, investigate it and help others learn.
careers.work: University and institute roles combine some mix of teaching, research, supervision, publication and extension. Project appointments can be temporary and tied to a specific grant.
careers.entry: Relevant MVSc and often PhD training support this route. NET, ARS, experience and discipline requirements depend on the employer and current notification; none guarantees an appointment.
careers.fit: You like explaining concepts, reading critically and working patiently through uncertain results.
careers.first: Ask to assist with a supervised literature review or small project. Learn research ethics, basic statistics and reference management.
careers.watch: Choose a supervisor and research environment carefully. Compare actual training, funding and methods experience rather than collecting qualifications alone.

careers.title: Pharma, vaccines & animal-health industry
careers.summary: Connect veterinary knowledge with products, evidence and customers.
careers.work: Possible roles include technical services, training, pharmacovigilance, regulatory support, diagnostics, product work and field sales. The daily balance of science, communication and commercial targets varies.
careers.entry: Entry criteria are employer-specific. BVSc graduates may fit some roles; research or specialist posts may require MVSc, PhD or prior experience.
careers.fit: You enjoy explaining science, solving client problems and collaborating with business teams.
careers.first: Compare three genuine job descriptions. Highlight the common technical, communication and travel requirements; build one relevant work sample.
careers.watch: Ask what is measured: sales, customer training, scientific work or project delivery. Product promotion still needs accurate, responsible communication.

careers.title: Wildlife, zoos & conservation
careers.summary: Animal health within conservation, rehabilitation and managed populations.
careers.work: Work may combine preventive medicine, quarantine, rescue, diagnostics, welfare and collaboration with keepers or conservation teams. Opportunities can be limited and project-based.
careers.entry: Clinical responsibilities require the appropriate veterinary qualification and registration. Relevant supervised wildlife experience and postgraduate study can matter, depending on the position.
careers.fit: You are interested in population health, welfare and working patiently in multidisciplinary teams.
careers.first: Seek a formally supervised placement through your college or an established organisation. Learn the safety and permit rules before any animal handling.
careers.watch: Wildlife work is not a shortcut to independent capture or treatment. Do not seek unsupervised handling experience.

careers.title: Shelter medicine & animal welfare
careers.summary: Improve welfare through prevention, accessible care and good systems.
careers.work: Shelter and NGO work can include population health, sterilisation programmes, outbreak prevention, records, community education and resource allocation.
careers.entry: BVSc & AH, applicable registration and supervised clinical competence underpin clinical posts. Programme management roles may ask for additional experience.
careers.fit: You like community work, teamwork and balancing individual care with population needs.
careers.first: Volunteer through a recognised supervised programme. Observe infection control, pain management, patient tracking and staff safety.
careers.watch: Ask about supervision, caseload limits, facilities and staff support. Compassion works best with safe, sustainable clinical systems.

careers.title: Practice ownership & veterinary ventures
careers.summary: Build a service around a real animal-health need.
careers.work: Routes include clinics, mobile services, farm consultancy and veterinary education or technology ventures. Running the service adds finance, operations and people management to veterinary work.
careers.entry: Clinical ventures need the relevant registration and local legal compliance. Business registration, premises, medicines, waste handling and other permissions depend on the service and location.
careers.fit: You enjoy responsibility, service design, communication and learning the business side.
careers.first: Interview five potential users before investing. Draft a simple service plan covering supervision, equipment, recurring costs, safety and referrals.
careers.watch: Revenue is not take-home pay. Price in rent, staffing, consumables, compliance, emergencies and time away from clinical work.

careers.title: Veterinary writing, education & health tech
careers.summary: Make sound veterinary knowledge useful beyond the consulting room.
careers.work: Work can include scientific content, education, product support, research communication, medical editing or health-data projects. Some positions combine these tasks with clinical or industry work.
careers.entry: A veterinary degree gives subject knowledge; employers also assess writing, evidence appraisal, teaching, data or product skills. Clinical advice remains subject to professional responsibilities.
careers.fit: You enjoy explaining complex ideas, checking sources and making useful things for other people.
careers.first: Create a small portfolio: one cited patient-education sheet, one evidence summary and one clear explainer. Remove all identifying case information.
careers.watch: Avoid unsupported health claims and invented citations. Develop a specific skill alongside veterinary knowledge rather than relying on a degree title alone.
